chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Saif, from Bakkar, who said:

My father asked him (meaning Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him), while I was listening: 'What is the limit of the illness that permits leaving the fast?' He said, 'When he is unable to eat the pre-dawn meal (suhoor).'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific medical condition that exempts a Muslim from fasting during Ramadan according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* provides a concrete, practical criterion for the exemption of illness (*marad*) in Shia jurisprudence, linking the physical capacity to perform *suhoor* directly to the validity of fasting. It reflects the Imami scholarly approach of deriving legal thresholds from observable physiological limitations, ensuring that the hardship of fasting does not become unbearable. This specific metric serves as a clear guideline for laypeople and jurists alike in determining when the obligation to fast is suspended.
